_about: Editorial guides for the website, in the spirit of Time Out itineraries and the NYT's 36 Hours. Restaurant facts come only from guide-data.json; attraction facts from attractions.json (with sources). Written Nov 26, 2026 for the Dec 2026–Feb 2027 season; re-check dated items before publishing. No offers, deals or implied partnerships (BRIEF.md).

guides.title: 36 Hours in Chinatown and Penn Quarter
guides.dek: A Friday-to-Sunday plan for the blocks around the Friendship Archway: two museums, a theater or a game, and noodles at every turn.
guides.intro: Chinatown proper covers barely a dozen blocks, and much of it has been sold to national chains. That is exactly why it rewards a plan. Within a ten-minute walk of the Friendship Archway sit two Smithsonian museums, the house where Lincoln was shot, three serious theaters and an NBA and NHL arena. Treat the neighborhood as the place you eat between them, and the weekend fills itself.

stops.title: Start under the arch
stops.text: Walk the 600 and 700 blocks of H Street first. Look up: city design rules require Chinese characters on every storefront, which is how the chains ended up with signs of their own. The On Leong and Hip Sing merchants' associations bought these buildings in the 1930s, after the first Chinatown on Pennsylvania Avenue was cleared.

stops.title: American Chinese, reworked
stops.text: Lucky Danger sits at 7th and D, three blocks south of Chinatown's official boundary. Tim Ma's kitchen treats General Tso's chicken and crab rangoon as dishes worth rethinking, and there are two cocktail bars. Book ahead on Fridays.

stops.title: A show
stops.text: Through January 10, A Midsummer Night's Dream plays Harman Hall. Woolly Mammoth's Hanukkah Spectacular runs through December 20, and from January 23 the Klein Theatre has A Raisin in the Sun. Or, if the Caps or Wizards are home, the arena is three minutes from the Archway.

stops.title: Cantonese after hours
stops.text: New Big Wong is the neighborhood's late room, down a flight of stairs on H Street and open until 3 a.m. on Fridays.

stops.title: Egg tarts at opening
stops.text: Joy Luck House opens at 10:30 a.m. Order from the glass case: warm egg tarts, mooncakes, a taro boba.

stops.title: Two museums, one building
stops.text: Doors open at 11:30 a.m. Give the Portrait Gallery's presidents an hour, then cross the courtyard to American art.

stops.title: Rice noodles before they run out
stops.text: China Boy is a daytime counter, done by 5 p.m. and closed Tuesdays. The order is the dry-fried beef chow fun, made with the house's own rice noodles.

stops.title: Ford's Theatre
stops.text: Timed entries run every half hour until 4 p.m. Same-day tickets are free at the box office; reserving online costs a small fee.

stops.title: Upstairs at Daikaya
stops.text: The second-floor izakaya does small plates, cocktails and Japanese whisky. Reserve on OpenTable, and leave the ramen for another day: it's served only downstairs.

stops.title: Or a game
stops.text: If the Caps or Wizards are home, the arena is three minutes from the Archway.

stops.title: Roast duck noodle soup
stops.text: Watch the noodles being pulled in Chinatown Express's front window on 6th Street, then order the roast duck noodle soup.

stops.title: A synagogue that moved
stops.text: Walk east to the Capital Jewish Museum. Admission is free with a suggested donation; bring ID if you're 18 or older.

stops.title: Beef noodles for the road
stops.text: Back on 6th Street, Cinnara builds its bowls on a slow-simmered beef bone broth. Try the Mala Spicy Beef Noodle Soup or the Taiwan Braised Beef Noodle Soup.

tips: Gallery Place–Chinatown Metro (Red, Green and Yellow lines) lets you out at the Archway.
Hours change. Check each place's page, linked from every stop, before you go.

guides.title: Game Night at Capital One Arena
guides.dek: Where to eat before puck drop or tipoff, and where to go after the final horn.
guides.intro: The arena takes up a whole block of Chinatown, so the neighborhood's best moves are minutes from your seat. Mid-renovation, the building is open but still changing. Eat before you go in, and keep a late-night plan in your pocket for afterward.

stops.title: Soup dumplings across H Street
stops.text: Luna Hall is a three-minute walk from the arena. Dumpling District's Rainbow Soup Dumplings platter (one of each flavor) is the quickest way to feed a group.

stops.title: Fried chicken and a drink
stops.text: TKK's tenders come original, crispy mild or crispy spicy. Wait for your order at Luna Bar, a few steps away.

stops.title: Hand-pulled lamen
stops.text: Reren, upstairs on 7th Street, pulls its noodles by hand and serves until 10 p.m. Its full bar also pours bubble tea.

stops.title: Bantam King
stops.text: The Daikaya team's chicken ramen and fried chicken, at 5th and G. Weekday happy hour runs from 5 to 7 p.m.

stops.title: The late-night standby
stops.text: New Big Wong serves Cantonese food until 2 a.m. Sunday to Thursday and 3 a.m. on Fridays and Saturdays.

stops.title: Pho at any hour
stops.text: Ambrosia stays open 24 hours from Thursday morning through Monday night, with pho, banh mi and wok dishes.

stops.title: Karaoke at Wok and Roll
stops.text: Next door to the restaurant, private karaoke rooms run until 3 a.m. on Fridays and Saturdays. Book a room ahead for a group.

tips: Check the arena's event page for door times and its bag policy before you leave.
Luna Hall, Reren, Ambrosia and Wok and Roll are all within five minutes of the arena's 7th Street side.

guides.title: Dinner and a Show
guides.dek: Penn Quarter has four stages within a ten-minute walk. Here's how to eat around them.
guides.intro: The Shakespeare Theatre Company has two houses here, Woolly Mammoth stages new work off 7th Street, and Ford's Theatre is a working playhouse as well as a historic site. Curtains are mostly at 7:30 or 8 p.m., which leaves room for an early dinner, or for a late one if you'd rather eat after the show.

stops.title: A Midsummer Night's Dream
stops.text: Simon Godwin directs Shakespeare's comedy at Harman Hall, across F Street from the arena.

stops.title: A Raisin in the Sun
stops.text: Tim Bond directs Lorraine Hansberry's play at the Klein Theatre, three blocks south on 7th Street. The run has been extended.

stops.title: Hanukkah Spectacular
stops.text: Woolly's holiday show was extended through December 20.

stops.title: Ford's Theatre
stops.text: See the season calendar on fords.org. Daytime visits to the historic site run until 4 p.m.

stops.title: Lucky Danger
stops.text: Its own pre-show pitch names Woolly, Ford's and the Shakespeare Theatre, and it's a short walk to all three. Reservations are suggested.

stops.title: Bantam King
stops.text: A fast, focused dinner: chicken ramen or fried chicken, with happy hour until 7 on weekdays.

stops.title: Daikaya Ramen Shop
stops.text: Sapporo-style ramen, walk-in only. Go early if your show starts at 7:30.

stops.title: Upstairs at Daikaya
stops.text: Japanese whisky and small plates, with DJs on weekends.

stops.title: New Big Wong
stops.text: Still serving long after the theaters empty out.

tips: Romeo and Juliet follows at the Klein Theatre, April 13 to May 16, 2027.

guides.title: An Afternoon at the Portrait Gallery
guides.dek: Two free Smithsonian museums under one roof, with a noodle lunch before and egg tarts after.
guides.intro: The National Portrait Gallery and the Smithsonian American Art Museum share one block at 8th and F, four minutes from the Archway. Both are free, both open at 11:30 a.m., and both stay open until 7 p.m. That late close is rare on the Mall and makes an afternoon here easy to plan.

stops.title: China Boy
stops.text: House-made rice noodles at a daytime counter. Closed Tuesdays.

stops.title: Chinatown Garden
stops.text: A long-running Cantonese and Hong Kong-style room on H Street.

stops.title: PHO 88 Noodles & Grill
stops.text: Vietnamese noodle soups, broken rice plates and Vietnamese coffee.

stops.title: National Portrait Gallery and American Art Museum
stops.text: Free, with no passes needed. Use the F Street or G Street entrance.

stops.title: The Holiday Market outside
stops.text: In December, F Street outside the museums fills with more than 115 vendors.

stops.title: National Building Museum
stops.text: Seven minutes east, the Great Hall is worth a look for its scale alone.

stops.title: Joy Luck House
stops.text: Egg tarts, mooncakes and taro boba. Closed Mondays.

stops.title: Tous les Jours
stops.text: The Korean bakery café inside Luna Hall.

stops.title: Sharetea
stops.text: Near the corner of 5th and H.

guides.title: Convention Day
guides.dek: Lunch in 20 minutes, a dinner table for 12, and somewhere still open at midnight, all within a 12-minute walk of the Convention Center.
guides.intro: Every walk time in this guide starts at the Convention Center's south side on Mount Vernon Square. Head south on 7th Street and you're in Chinatown in about five minutes. These are the moves for a day of sessions and badges.

stops.title: Reren Lamen & Bar
stops.text: The closest sit-down meal: hand-pulled noodles and dumplings.

stops.title: Kura Revolving Sushi Bar
stops.text: Sushi on a conveyor belt. Quick if you're eating alone.

stops.title: Luna Hall
stops.text: Soup dumplings, poke and fried chicken under one roof. Dumpling District and Poke Ninja take online orders through Luna Hall.

stops.title: China Boy
stops.text: Rice noodles to go. Daytime only, closed Tuesdays.

stops.title: Lucky Danger
stops.text: Book the dining room on OpenTable. For a team event, the mahjong room hosts private classes for up to 15 with three weeks' notice.

stops.title: Wok and Roll
stops.text: Dinner, then private karaoke rooms next door, booked separately.

stops.title: The Izakaya at Daikaya
stops.text: Small plates for a table that wants to share. Reserve on OpenTable.

stops.title: Luna Bar
stops.text: Luna Hall's lounge can be booked for events.

stops.title: Ambrosia
stops.text: Open around the clock from Thursday through Monday night.

stops.title: New Big Wong
stops.text: Cantonese until 2 or 3 a.m.

stops.title: Sixth & I
stops.text: Check its calendar for author talks and concerts a block from the Archway.

tips: Many places in this guide take online orders. Use the Order online filter on the Places page.
